title: Jewellery brand GIVA raises Rs 975 crore as it aims to cross 1,000 outlets in the next 3-5 years
summary: Jewellery brand GIVA raises Rs 975 crore to expand retail footprint
detailed: Bengaluru-based jewellery brand GIVA has raised more than $100 million (about Rs 975 crore) in a funding round led by Multiples Alternate Asset Management and its co-investors.

sentences: Bengaluru-based jewellery brand GIVA has raised more than $100 million (about Rs 975 crore) in a funding round led by Multiples Alternate Asset Management and its co-investors.
Existing investors Epiq Capital and Edelweiss Discovery Fund also took part.
The round includes primary capital, secondary transactions in which existing shareholders sell their stakes, and ESOP buyback.

Early investors India Quotient and Sixth Sense Ventures are partly exiting but keeping some of their holding, and Multiples will get a seat on GIVA's board
The brand said the money will go towards strengthening its leadership team, building manufacturing capabilities and opening more physical stores, calling the deal the largest investment yet in India's new-age jewellery market.

“ Multiples' backing is a strong endorsement of what we have built at GIVA since 2019, a high-growth, design-led fine jewellery brand that Indian consumers trust for everyday wear and gifting, ” said Ishendra Agarwal, founder and CEO of GIVA.

“ As we enter our next phase, we are focused on scaling our omnichannel presence, strengthening our manufacturing capabilities and elevating the fine jewellery experience for modern Indian consumers, ” he added.
GIVA runs around 425 stores across India and Sri Lanka.
It plans to add 160 in FY27, with more focus on Tier II and III cities, and aims to cross 1,000 outlets in the next three to five years.
About 70% of its stores are in metros.
Agarwal said the company will deepen its presence in Lucknow, Dehradun, Kanpur and Surat and enter markets such as Agra.
Physical stores bring in about 45% of revenue today, with the rest coming from its own website and app and from third-party e-commerce and quick commerce platforms.
Agarwal expects the offline share to reach 75-80% within three years.
On manufacturing, GIVA outsources bulk production but does plating, finishing, customised and made-to-order pieces in-house.
It will invest in these capabilities in Jaipur and Mumbai.
Founded in 2019 by Agarwal, Nikita Prasad and Sachin Shetty, GIVA started online as a 925 sterling silver jewellery brand and later added gold and lab-grown diamond jewellery.
Silver still accounts for around 60% of revenue, with gold and lab-grown diamonds making up the rest.
Its average selling price is about Rs 3,500 for silver pieces and Rs 15,000-18,000 for lab-grown diamond jewellery, and its blended average order value is about Rs 5,000.
The company plans to stock more products in the Rs 10,000-40,000 range.
It is also building out its men's range, which makes up about 20% of its silver business, and recently launched a demi-fine jewellery brand called Ixia.
Agarwal said GIVA aims to be ready for an IPO within two to three years, though a listing is at least three years away.
Notably, GIVA claims to have grown at over 70% CAGR over the last three years and ended FY26 with revenue of around Rs 865 crore.
Agarwal said the negative EBITDA margin shrank from double digits to single digits in FY26, and that stores open for more than a year are profitable.
GIVA expects to post a net profit in FY28.
It aims to be IPO-ready in two to three years, though a listing is at least three years away, he said.
GIVA raised Rs 530 crore in a Series C funding round led by Creaegis in June 2025, with Premji Invest, Epiq Capital and Edelweiss Discovery Fund participating.
In February this year, it raised Rs 110 crore (around $12 million) in a Series C extension led by HPV CC1 Ltd.
In May, it raised Rs 270 crore in debt through a multi-tranche round of debentures led by BlackSoil Capital, with InCred Credit Fund, Stride Ventures and Nuvama Crossover Yield Opportunities Fund.
Multiples' portfolio includes Licious, ACKO, PVR and Arvind Fashions.
In 2025, the private equity firm closed a $430 million continuation fund co-led by LGT Capital Partners, HarbourVest Partners, Hamilton Lane and TPG NewQuest.
